contentText: Venezuela's acting president offered on Sunday to collaborate with the United States ⁠on an agenda focused on "shared development", striking a conciliatory tone for the first time since U.S. forces captured the oil-rich nation's president, Nicolas Maduro. The US captured him his wife in a military operation Saturday. Trump said the US would “run” Venezuela temporarily, but Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday that it would not govern the country day-to-day other than enforcing an existing " oil quarantine." Details and analysis by FRANCE 24's Andrew Hilliar.
